subject: Drafting: breach notification & cooperation — DPA clause
messages:
From: Julia Martin <dpo@finhealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinHealth Legal <legal@finhealth.com>, security@finhealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:02:00 +0100
Subject: Clarifying breach-notify timing & cooperation language in the DPA

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the DPA draft. Before we progress to signatures, Legal and Security have a couple of non-negotiable items on incident response I need to clarify:

1) Notification timing: per GDPR, our board expects Controller-level notification to regulators within 72 hours of becoming aware. From a customer control perspective, we (the Controller) require Processor (Redwood) to provide initial written notice to us no later than 48 hours after Redwood becomes aware of a confirmed or suspected personal data breach affecting FinHealth data.

2) Scope of "cooperation": we need explicit commitments that Redwood will (a) preserve and provide logs and telemetry related to the incident, (b) provide reasonable access for our forensic vendor under an NDA, and (c) deliver a post-incident root-cause analysis and mitigation plan within 30 days.

3) Evidence: please provide an SOC 2 Type II report (redacted ok) and the last security third-party penetration test summary.

I've attached our standard breach checklist so you can see the items Legal expects us to get from processors. If Redwood cannot commit to the 48-hour initial notice, please propose alternative language that is specific and measurable.

Can we schedule a short call this week to align?

Thanks,
Julia Martin
Data Protection Officer
FinHealth Inc.

Attachment: finhealth_breach_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Martin <dpo@finhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying breach-notify timing & cooperation language in the DPA

Hi Julia — thanks for the checklist and clear ask. High level response and proposed compromise below (we attached a redline of the DPA with these edits).

Short answer: Redwood is committed to fast, transparent cooperation. We cannot guarantee an exact clock-start for regulator-facing filings (those are the Controller's decision and depend on facts), but we can and will: 

- Provide initial written notice to the Controller within 72 hours of Redwood becoming aware of a confirmed personal data breach affecting customer data, including a summary of impacted data categories, estimated scope, and known mitigations at time of notice.
- If Redwood reasonably suspects a breach but cannot confirm within 72 hours, we will send an interim notice within 72 hours describing the suspected nature and the steps we're taking, and follow up with confirmation or correction as soon as possible.
- Deliver a post-incident report (findings, mitigations, timeline) within 30 days of confirmation, and make logs/telemetry available to the Controller's designated forensic vendor under a mutual NDA.

Suggested clause language (redline attached):
"Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay and no later than seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a confirmed personal data breach affecting Controller Personal Data. Where Processor is unable to provide full details within 72 hours, Processor will provide an initial notification containing available information and will provide updates as more information becomes available. Processor will provide Controller with reasonable cooperation including access to logs and telemetry, and a post-incident written report within thirty (30) days after confirmation of the breach."

We don't accept a blanket 48-hour confirmation requirement because confirmation timelines vary (e.g., multi-tenant detection, staged investigations). However, we are open to including a firm 48-hour "acknowledgement" commitment (i.e., Redwood will acknowledge receipt of any Controller inquiry or alert within 48 hours) in addition to the 72-hour initial notice for confirmed breaches.

On evidence: we will provide a SOC 2 Type II summary and can share the full report under a Mutual NDA. Our SOC 2 Type II (period: 10/2025–09/2026) summary is attached as SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf. We will also provide the latest third-party penetration test summary.

I'll leave technical for Rishi and legal details for Karthik — proposed call: Friday 10/30 14:00 UTC?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v2_redlines.docx (redline), SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (PDF)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Julia Martin <dpo@finhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying breach-notify timing & cooperation language in the DPA

Julia / Neha — quick note from Legal/AM side:

- We prefer the 72-hour initial notice as a processor standard for EU customers (consistent with how many processor DPAs are written). However, to address FinHealth's operational need, we're willing to include a carve-out that requires Redwood to provide an "acknowledgement of investigation" within 48 hours of detection (not confirmation) and to escalate to a named security liaison.
- "Reasonable cooperation" should be defined with examples and limits: e.g., Redwood will provide relevant logs and telemetry related to the incident, subject to its obligations to preserve multi-tenant confidentiality and to any legal/regulatory constraints. For forensic access, Redwood will permit a third-party forensic vendor to review relevant sanitized evidence under a scoped NDA and only in Redwood-managed environments.
- For HIPAA workloads (if that becomes relevant), we will include language referencing Business Associate obligations and specific PHI handling.

Proposed tweak to Neha's redline: replace "reasonable cooperation" with "cooperation as set forth in Schedule 3 (Incident Cooperation), which shall include examples and a process for evidence sharing." We'll draft Schedule 3 and circulate.

— Karthik
General Counsel (interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Julia Martin <dpo@finhealth.com>

Cc: FinHealth Legal <legal@finhealth.com>, security@finhealth.com, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarifying breach-notify timing & cooperation language in the DPA

Neha / Karthik — appreciate the quick replies and the SOC 2 summary; we're reviewing. A few points from FinHealth Legal/Security:

- 48-hour acknowledgement vs 72-hour initial notification: acknowledgement is helpful but not sufficient for regulator comfort. Our preference remains an explicit 48-hour customer-facing notification for incidents where Controller Personal Data is confirmed to be impacted. If Redwood requires 72 hours to "confirm," we need stronger interim obligations (timestamped logs of actions taken, named Redwood security contact, cadence of updates).

- Forensic vendor access: FinHealth's forensic vendor must be permitted to ingest logs and run limited analyses against Redwood-provided telemetry; this must be done under explicit scope and a mutual NDA. Please confirm Redwood's willingness to allow data extraction to a sandboxed environment for our vendor, limited to our tenancy.

- Evidence delivery: we will require delivery of a post-incident report with root cause and mitigation steps within 30 days; if root cause is expected to take longer, provide an interim remediation timeline.

Can we take the call Friday as proposed (10/30) or move to Monday 11/02 if Redwood needs internal approval? Our security lead will join.

Best regards,
Julia Martin
DPO, FinHealth Inc.

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying breach-notify timing & cooperation language in the DPA

Julia — thanks. Quick confirmations and next steps:

- Call scheduled: Monday 02 Nov 2026, 15:00 UTC (we'll send a calendar invite).
- Redwood accepts: 72-hour initial notice for confirmed breaches, plus a 48-hour acknowledgement/ack receipt of reports/alerts from the Controller (we'll capture both in the DPA).
- Forensic access: Redwood will allow a scoped forensic review by Controller's vendor under a mutual NDA and in a sandboxed environment limited to the Controller's tenancy. Redwood will not permit broad unrestricted extraction from multi-tenant systems; any extracts will be scoped and sanitized.
- Post-incident report: Redwood commits to a 30-day post-incident report where feasible; if root-cause requires additional time, Redwood will provide an interim findings summary and an expected delivery schedule for the full RCA.

Attachments in prep for the call: redwood_dpa_v2_redlines.docx (with the new 48/72 language), SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf, and our proposed Schedule 3 (Incident Cooperation) draft. We'll circulate the call invite and a short agenda (timing, forensic scope, evidence sharing, NDA).

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on Monday.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
